title: Greening the Former Basirih Landfill: Care for 2,500 Trees Continues Through the Dry Season
excerpt: PT Pelindo Regional 3, DLH Banjarmasin, and Relawan Nusantara are caring for 2,500 trees at the former Basirih TPA (landfill) during the dry season. Take a look at the strategy and the preparations for replanting!
seoTitle: Greening the Former Basirih Landfill Goes On - Relawan Nusantara
seoDescription: PT Pelindo Regional 3, DLH Banjarmasin, and Relawan Nusantara care for 2,500 trees at the former Basirih landfill in the dry season. See the strategy and plans!
html:
Planting trees is the first step in restoring the environment. But keeping seedlings growing amid hot weather and limited water is the next challenge in the effort to green the former Basirih TPA (landfill) area in Banjarmasin.

The program to plant 2,500 tree seedlings carried out by PT Pelabuhan Indonesia (Pelindo) Regional 3 Banjarmasin, the Banjarmasin City Environmental Agency (DLH Banjarmasin), and Relawan Nusantara has now entered the maintenance phase. This ongoing collaboration aims to care for the plants while preparing for replanting in the rainy season. Based on monitoring results in September 2026, the seedling survival rate stood at around 30–40 percent, still below the initial target of 70–80 percent.

These monitoring results became the basis for strengthening the care of the plants that are still surviving and for preparing replacement planting.

The Dry Season Poses a Challenge to Tree Growth

The former Basirih landfill area has its own environmental challenges in the restoration process. After planting, seedling growth is still affected by soil conditions, water availability, and the weather around the site.

Monitoring results in September 2026 showed that extreme heat, rising soil temperatures caused by the decomposition of waste beneath the surface, and limited water sources were among the factors affecting seedling survival.

These conditions show that greening requires sustained attention after planting. Besides making sure the seedlings are properly planted, care is also needed to help the plants cope with changing environmental conditions.

Strengthening Care Amid Limited Water

To keep the plants alive, the facilitator team, together with 20 volunteers and related parties, has taken a number of mitigation measures. These efforts include optimizing watering using the alternative water sources available, moving plants to more supportive areas, and providing care through a drip-watering system and routine watering in the morning and afternoon.

These steps are taken to help the plants meet their water needs during the dry season, while giving the seedlings that are still surviving a better chance of growing.

The program facilitator, Mustaqim, explained that replacement planting, or the replacing of dead seedlings, has not yet been carried out. Replanting is planned to take place all at once when the rainy season arrives, so that water is more readily available and the replacement seedlings have a better chance of survival.

400 Seedlings Prepared for Replacement Planting

In addition to strengthening maintenance, the team is also preparing follow-up steps to support the success of the program. Around 400 reserve seedlings have been prepared to replace the plants that died once conditions become more favorable.

The preparations also include repairing the drip-watering system and meeting supporting needs, such as organic fertilizer and mulch, to help improve the condition of the soil and retain its moisture.

With these steps, the greening program focuses not only on planting, but also on ensuring that every effort already made receives ongoing care.

Sustaining the Greening Effort in Banjarmasin

The greening program at the former Basirih landfill is part of a shared endeavor to improve environmental quality and encourage the restoration of a former final disposal site. The challenge of the dry season is a reminder that greening land takes time, perseverance, and continuous care.

The support of the community and stakeholders is an important asset in sustaining this program. Through collaboration and the right maintenance measures, the hope is that more and more trees can grow and benefit the environment in the long term.

Let us take part in supporting acts of kindness so that more environmental restoration efforts can be carried out and bring benefits for the future. Let us support the greening effort by planting trees for Indonesia's forests.

Luaskan Manfaat
